generator_metadata.summary: BG-colored grid (h ∈ 7-30, w ∈ 7-30, by difficulty) painted uniformly with one bg color fixed to 0, containing: (a) ONE SOLID RECTANGLE of size rh × rw (rh ∈ 5..h-2, rw ∈ 5..w-2, both ≥5) at random interior position (rr, rc) with ≥1-cell margin from all grid edges, painted in rect_color (distinct from 0). (b) AT THE RECTANGLE'S FOUR INSIDE-CORNER CELLS — (rr+1, rc+1), (rr+1, rc+rw-2), (rr+rh-2, rc+1), (rr+rh-2, rc+rw-2) — paint 4 DISTINCT non-{0, rect_color} colors drawn from {0..9}. Rule (CLEAR THE FOUR INSIDE CORNERS (SET TO BACKGROUND 0) AND PLACE THE 4 CORNER COLORS AT THE FOUR DIAGONALLY-OPPOSITE OUTSIDE CORNERS OF THE RECTANGLE): IDENTIFY the rectangle (solid rect_color region) and its 4 inside-corner cells with their distinct colors c0, c1, c2, c3 (TL, TR, BL, BR of inside). CLEAR the 4 inside-corner marker cells to background 0, leaving four holes in the rectangle. PAINT the 4 OUTSIDE-CORNER cells of the rectangle: (rr-1, rc-1)=c3 (diagonally opposite TL→BR-corner), (rr-1, rc+rw)=c2 (TR→BL), (rr+rh, rc-1)=c1 (BL→TR), (rr+rh, rc+rw)=c0 (BR→TL). Net: inside colors jump to the diagonally-opposite outside corners while their former cells become background.

review_brief:
# Review summary

Both assigned targets now have repaired base sources and complete task-local
native parametric deliverables. All labels cited below were replayed through the
packet's protected Racket runtime. These are authoring receipts, not owner
qualification, acceptance, or training admission.

## `e6cf1120a17d`

The base description contradicted its canonical executable rule: it said the
four inset markers were restored to rectangle color, while the program clears
them to background `0`. The source summary and task documentation now match the
executable behavior. The ordinary generator also reaches the lawful 30×30 grid
with a 28×28 rectangle while preserving the one-cell outside-corner margin.

The parametric family preserves the byte-exact canonical diagonal permutation
and adds `min_color_turn`. Step A locates the smallest marker and derives a turn
from its quadrant; step B clears all inset markers and routes every color using
that turn. A protected wrong-turn witness changes the result on an
anti-diagonal case. Two demonstrations cover both turns and identify each
setting against the finite declared family. Four queries include 30×30.

## `8a761b80b11b`

The base generator declared controls it never consumed, rejected otherwise
legal explicit dimensions inside difficulty bands, could silently underfill the
requested run count, and hard-coded degenerate sizes. The repaired sampler uses
only honest controls, rejects unknown/stale overrides, honors full legal size
overrides for every difficulty, constructs the exact run count, makes palette
selection visible in the grid, and sizes every degenerate probe from the same
validated dimensions.

The parametric family preserves the byte-exact endpoint rule and adds
`longest_color_gate`. Step A finds the unique longest horizontal run and selects
its color. Step B keeps endpoints for every run of that color and centers for
all other runs. Generated scenes force the anchor color to recur, force the
first run to have another color, exercise odd and even centers, and include a
substantive 30×30 query. A protected first-run-anchor counterfactual changes the
output.

## Verification retained

- Focused suites: 21/21 and 32/32 tests.
- Two exact-source authoring preflights: passed, 32 protected-Racket evaluations
  each, including canonical originals and all settings.
- Two protected causal builds plus fresh source

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The selected marker color, its clockwise quadrant index, and the resulting clockwise/counterclockwise turn.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Locate the smallest of the four inset marker colors and determine whether its quadrant lies on the main or anti diagonal.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Clear all four inset markers, then route every marker color to the adjacent outside corner in the turn selected by step A.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The destination permutation is chosen from the input-dependent minimum-marker quadrant; choosing the wrong turn changes every outside-corner assignment on anti-diagonal cases.
